title: From Evaluation to Defense: Advancing Safety in Video Large Language Models
measurement_description: The paper measures the safety of Video Large Language Models, specifically their propensity to generate harmful responses to video-query pairs. This includes the detection of content that promotes hate or violence based on religion, as a sub-component of the 'Hate Speech' and 'Violent/Hateful Organizations' risk categories.
findings: The paper's key finding is that integrating video modality significantly degrades the safety performance of Large Language Models, making them more susceptible to generating harmful content. This vulnerability extends to categories that include religious-based harm, such as 'Hate Speech' and 'Violent, Hate Groups and Individuals'. The proposed defense framework, VideoSafety-R1, was shown to effectively mitigate these risks and restore safety performance without compromising video understanding capabilities.
